scenarios.label: Agent acting for users via X API
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent posts, reads or sends DMs for each end user through OAuth 2.0 user-context on the standard X API.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; see c1-c8

waiting.basis: No official timeline found. A vendor blog says immediate to several days; one 2020 blog reports over a month and a rejection (c20, c21).

scenarios.approval: No app review for outside users was found in the docs, but the dossier did not confirm this either way. Developer account setup needs a use-case description.
extras: Credits bought upfront; deducted per request

modifiers.note: Credits bought upfront; deducted per request

scenarios.label: Ads API beyond basic app permissions
scenarios.when_this_applies: Your agent uses X Ads API endpoints that need Standard Access.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured; see c13-c17

waiting.basis: No timeline found for Standard Access.

scenarios.approval: Apps with limited app-level permissions must apply for Standard Access through an X representative. What X checks was not found.

prerequisites.title: X account and developer account
prerequisites.detail: Sign in to console.x.com with an X account, accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, and describe how you will use the API.

prerequisites.title: Prepaid API credits
prerequisites.detail: The X API is pay-per-usage; you buy credits in the Developer Console and requests deduct from them.

prerequisites.title: An X representative contact
prerequisites.detail: Standard Access for the Ads API and any increase of the user token limit both go through an X representative.

steps.title: Create developer account
steps.detail: Sign in at console.x.com, accept the agreement and describe your use of the API.

steps.title: Buy API credits
steps.detail: Purchase credits in the Developer Console; payment details are needed.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Click New App and enter a name, description and use case.

steps.title: Save client ID and secret
steps.detail: Credentials show only once; store them in a vault. Regenerating invalidates the old ones.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret stored securely

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Use Composio's API to create a custom auth config with your client ID and secret, then copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the X app settings. Request minimal scopes only.
steps.done_when: A test user completes the consent flow

steps.title: Apply for Ads Standard Access
steps.detail: Contact your X representative to apply for Standard Access.

traps.title: Account suspension during testing
traps.detail: Developers report sudden suspensions after a few test posts, with unspent credits stuck and appeals rejected in general terms. Test with few, ordinary posts.

traps.title: Credentials shown only once
traps.detail: If you lose them you must regenerate, which invalidates the old ones and breaks any Composio auth config using them.

traps.title: Rate limits and costs are separate
traps.detail: You can stay within rate limits and still pay, or hit limits at no extra cost. Pay-per-usage is capped at 3 million Post reads per month.

traps.title: Token cap and fixed rate limits on Ads API
traps.detail: Pre-July 2023 Ads apps may be capped at 5 user tokens; raising it needs a representative. X does not increase Ads API rate limits.

blockers.what_it_means: Reports range from immediate approval to over a month ending in rejection; these are anecdotes, not official.
blockers.what_to_do: Give a specific, honest use-case description and resubmit if needed.

blockers.what_it_means: Developers report unexplained suspensions with credits left on the account.
blockers.what_to_do: Appeal to X and avoid repeated test posts.

open_questions: Does X require any review before outside users can authorize a standard X API app? Check docs.x.com or ask X developer support.
Does a customer's admin need to approve the app? The docs only describe the 3-legged flow per user; confirm with X.
What is the exact Standard Access timeline and review criteria for the Ads API? Ask your X representative.
What are current X API rate limits and the pay-per-usage limits for user-context calls? The rate-limit page was not retrievable.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked x.com, x.com.

evidence.answer: You can check whether Composio provides the OAuth app for a given toolkit on the Managed OAuth apps page.

evidence.question: C1
evidence.quote: Use your own credentials for toolkits where users see consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and Composio managed auth for the rest.
evidence.answer: You can mix approaches: use your own credentials for toolkits with user-facing consent screens (GitHub, Google, Slack) and managed auth for the rest; each toolkit gets its own auth config.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: アプリの申込み（申請）から1か月以上たって、ようやく審査結果が来ました。結果は不合格です。
evidence.answer: A 2020 developer blog reports the X developer application took over a month to get a result, and the result was a rejection (a single anecdote from the COVID-era period).

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: How long: varies from immediate to several days. There's no published SLA and no queue position to check.
evidence.answer: A third-party API vendor's blog (a competitor with a commercial interest) says developer approval takes from immediate to several days, with no published SLA.

evidence.question: R1
evidence.quote: After three of those posts, my account was instantly suspended, with paid credits remaining stuck on that particular account.
evidence.answer: Developers report account suspensions without explanation during API testing, including from test posts on pay-per-use plans, and appeals were reportedly rejected in general terms, so account suspension is a common blocker.
